story.thread: The signature thread is a SINGLE motion metaphor forged in the hero and reused as the page's grammar, not a color. Ponpon = scroll-is-a-playhead / physics-you-shove; Warhol = pop-art canvases that react to the cursor; DICH = color-temperature chapters + a 3D companion that follows you; Exat = distance-from-cursor drives type; Cuberto = one expo-out curve resolving every fill/roll/cursor. Winners bind visibly different mechanics (button fill, link roll, figure zoom, cursor state) to ONE shared law — one easing family + one color rule + one loud/quiet hierarchy per element class — so density reads as choreography, not noise. Re-fire the same metaphor hero->close: Ponpon's physics is still live at the About close; Warhol re-fires its cursor-reaction metaphor at both the Elvis section and the footer trail (two section-local instances, not one persistent channel, with page-wide scroll reveals filling the gaps); Cuberto's curve resolves the contact-reprise fill.
story.copy: The motion argues; the copy labels. One-clause heroes, caps micro-labels, attitude lists over credentials, warm imperatives at CTAs, '->' on acquisition CTAs, zero feature-benefit padding. Winner quotes calibrate specificity (imitate the refusal-to-explain, never the wording): Exat 'strikes a balance between form and function, neutrality and character' (one clause does all the explaining); Cuberto 'Digital design & development agency' (the whole pitch in four words); Eloy 'maximalist, little monster, a latinx baddie, kitsch, brat' (attitude list, zero credentials); compliance chrome stays in character ('Hey you [sparkle] this site uses cookies', lowercase accept/decline). Self-narration ('we craft immersive experiences') is the tell that kills the score even when craft is high — the copy names, the motion does the arguing.

spectacle_model.hero: The hero fires the first-impression spectacle hard (verdict forms in ~50ms and halos the rest of the score), rendering the thread as reusable motion vocabulary: Ponpon cover = live physics + character intro; Warhol = SplitText scale 0->1 with a warm single-hue array (#FB4E2B ×7 + a lighter #FFE5D5 final char — NOT a multi-hue color-cycle), back.out, 0.1s stagger, post-preloader; DICH = preloader-mood-gate handing into color-chapter one; Exat = the cursor-proximity glyph grid itself. But in THIS archetype the hero is NOT necessarily where the single climax sits — see continuation.

ARCHETYPE-SPECIFIC REFINEMENT 1 — the single peak is NOT hero-bound: Exat's climax is the mid-page specimen grid, Eloy's is the closing connect-CTA clone-storm, Cuberto's is ~30% down. The hero still fires hard for first-impression, but the narrative places the peak where the payoff logic wants it (specimen grid, lineup, finale). This is the archetype's departure from the hero-peak default.

ARCHETYPE-SPECIFIC REFINEMENT 2 — this archetype carries a very high continuation floor: winners run multiple always-on channels (per-class hover states + display-type effects + cursor field/trail + one idle channel + scroll texture). The floor is not micro (as it is for editorial/B2B) — it is dense-but-graded, sitting just below the peak. The specific '4-5 channels' count is a corpus-derived heuristic, not a scored rubric — see unverified.

Ponpon's chaptered scenes are the boundary case that most stresses the cap — like Bruno Simon's continuous driving, the panel scenes read as near-equal repeating peaks rather than one-peak-then-sub-peak. The cap holds only because each scene is the SAME mechanic re-fired, not a new competing spectacle.
spectacle_model.recommended_law: Bold-Maximal Spectacle-Momentum Law (a synthesized heuristic — the peak-count cap is a corpus observation; the channel-floor count is extrapolated, see unverified). Fire ONE signature spectacle (peak count capped at one) and place it where the payoff logic wants it — the hero for first-impression-led builds (Warhol, Ponpon cover), but freely mid-page (Exat specimen grid, Cuberto featured projects) or at the close (Eloy connect-CTA clone-storm) when the narrative earns it; the hero must still fire hard regardless, because ~50ms + halo. Then NEVER fall below the maximal floor: 4-5 continuous channels — per-element-class hover states, one display-type effect, one cursor field OR trail, one idle channel, one scroll texture — all bound to ONE easing family + ONE color rule + ONE loud/quiet hierarchy per element class, so density reads as choreography not noise. The continuation floor here runs dense-but-graded (never micro, never zero) — among the highest observed across the corpus, an extrapolation not a measured cross-archetype ranking; a silent section betrays the premise. The peak re-fires the SAME mechanic rather than introducing a competing second spectacle. Degrade the peak to a strong static/composed frame under reduced-motion; keep the transform/opacity/scroll channels alive; kill cursor fields to static grids on touch.

algorithm.decide: Name the ONE motion metaphor (the fil rouge) before any layout — a mechanic-concept bound to a single input, not a palette.
algorithm.rule: Pick a single primary driver the whole page obeys — one input mapped to one verb: scroll-position-is-a-playhead (Ponpon), cursor-distance-drives-type (Exat), cursor-position-reshapes-canvases (Warhol), section-enter-rotates-color (DICH), one-expo-curve-resolves-every-transition (Cuberto). Executable check: enumerate every planned mechanic and confirm each binds to that SAME primary input (or, for the curve-driven case, the same easing family); any mechanic bound to a different primary input is décor, not signature — cap décor at one secondary channel. Everything downstream reuses THIS input.

algorithm.decide: Forge the signature thread AS reusable vocabulary + commit ONE easing family and ONE color rule.
algorithm.rule: Choose one easing camp and never mix: elastic/back.out (Warhol back.out(2), Ponpon elastic.out(0.7,0.7)) OR expo-out (Cuberto cubic-bezier .16,1,.3,1) — not both. Color rule is binary: SATURATED register = 4-6 hues, each with a fixed role OR rotated one-per-section (DICH — sourced to a SINGLE corpus winner, see the section-accent-rotation gap; also Figma); KINETIC register = restrained palette where the TYPE motion is the maximalism (Mat Voyce cream, 21 TSI B&W, Exat blue->red 2-hue). Most of the corpus lives in the kinetic register — do not treat per-section color rotation as the default. Fills resolve to FULL role colors, never tints. Background register is an expression choice, not a definition.

algorithm.rule: Per section: hero display slot -> characterful SplitText (color-cycle/random-skew-elastic, NOT the monochrome line mask); figure grids -> contained zoom 1.1 + companion cue with from:'random' graded stagger; index/chapter rows -> spotlight (hovered lights, siblings dim 45%); the one spectacle section -> the signature mechanic (cursor-proximity typefield / operable specimen / physics scene / clone-storm). algorithm.decide: Set the per-element-class interaction states (hover / tap / focus) with amplitudes.
algorithm.rule: CTA: hover = full-token flood or rising-dome-fill + label inversion (Cuberto dome 0.5s cubic-bezier(.4,0,0,1), leading edge border-radius 50% 50% 0 0; solid variant = darker-same-hue shift, never paler), OR magnetic pull (label/button translates toward the cursor within a proximity radius, elastic-settle on leave — a distinct mechanic; commit one signature per build); tap = press/flash 90-160ms; focus-visible = mirror hover. LINK: hover LOUD = skewed text-roll (translateY -105% + skewY 0<->7deg, 1.2s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1)) on nav/overlay labels; hover QUIET = scaleX(0->1) underline (1s .16,1,.3,1) on utility/footer; tap = instant color swap. FIGURE: hover = zoom 1.1 (felt, never 1-3% twitch) + tint/scrim/caption-rise; tap = enlarge or caption reveal. INDEX_ROW: hover = accent rule + surfaced meta, siblings dim to 45%. HEADING: hover ONLY on interactive headings (Exat design-space morph, Warhol Elvis cursor-font-size) — NEVER on prose/numbers; entrance = characterful SplitText. NAV: transparent fixed bar that NEVER solidifies to an opaque brand-border bar; per-char roll or scramble on links; menu-open = full-viewport curtain. CURSOR: custom pointer chrome on pointer:fine only (see element_states.cursor).
evidence: Cuberto live CSS: dome-fill CTA, skewY 7deg link peel, scaling underline, contextual cursor — all one expo family

DICH: scramble section-nav + three section-swapped cursor variants; Mat Voyce: per-letter roll nav; nav never solidifies (Ponpon transparent after scroll)

algorithm.decide: Set the mobile / touch answer — dormant pointer classes, live press + scroll.
algorithm.rule: Cursor fields degrade to STATIC grids on touch (Exat explicit: 'touch devices receive static grid versions'); cursor trails/parallax and the custom cursor chrome go dormant/hidden. Press-class elements answer the tap with a flash floor 90-160ms. Depth that came from the pointer now comes from SCROLL. Swap the desktop hold-and-drag gallery for a native scroll-snap swipe track (tap-to-enlarge). Kinetic type keeps its scroll-driven channel; the peak degrades to a strong composed frame, never a sub-30fps render. Any audio stays muted until an explicit gesture (see the sound-channel gap).

cta.hover: Full-token flood or rising-dome-fill + label inversion — Cuberto pill (border-radius:1000px, overflow:hidden) holds a fill parked at translateY(101%) with a domed leading edge (border-radius:50% 50% 0 0) that rises + flattens, transition transform 0.5s cubic-bezier(.4,0,0,1); solid variant floods a full token (0.5s Power3.easeOut, retract 0.4s) and inverts the icon. Solid-brand builds shift DARKER same-hue (never paler tint). Pair a label swap-slide synced to the fill. SECOND committed option = MAGNETIC pull: the button (or its label) translates toward the cursor within a proximity radius on mousemove and elastic-settles back on leave — a distinct mechanic from the fill; commit ONE signature per build. (Cuberto dome-fill + magnetic amplitudes are carried-verified from a prior live-CSS read, not re-fetched this run — see unverified.)
cta.tap: The fill IS the tap answer on touch (press-driven), or a hard-press offset-shadow collapse at 125ms; flash floor 90-160ms. Magnetic pull is a no-op on touch (no pointer to attract to).
cta.focus: focus-visible mirrors hover exactly (full flood + inversion) — the fill is reachable by keyboard.

link.hover: LOUD (nav/overlay labels): skewed text-roll — label + duplicate in a clipped box translate -105% while each layer resolves skewY(0deg)<->skewY(7deg), transition transform 1.2s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1); the 7deg skew lifts it above a plain vertical roll. QUIET (utility/footer): pseudo-element underline scaleX(0->1), transition 1s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1). Per-char rollover (split-rollover) is the nav variant.
link.tap: Instant accent color swap (no roll on touch); underline snaps to full.
link.focus: Underline wipe + accent recolor on focus-visible; roll on nav links keeps an accessible name via aria-label.

figure.hover: Contained zoom to 1.1 (felt, never a 1-3% twitch) + a companion cue — tint, scrim lift, or caption rise; on dense grids the spotlight variant sharpens the hovered figure while siblings blur/dim (focus-defocus, keep galleries <~10 items).
figure.tap: Tap-to-enlarge (Awwwards Mobile Excellence line) or caption reveal; the zoom does not fire on touch.
figure.focus: focus-within triggers the same zoom + cue so keyboard users reach the caption.

index_row.hover: Hovered row lights with an accent rule + surfaced metadata while siblings dim to 45% (index-row-hover spotlight); chapter tiles add snap-to-place feedback.
index_row.tap: Row highlights on tap-active; meta stays visible (no hover-only content trapped).
index_row.focus: Same spotlight on focus-visible; the row is a real <a> so focus order is preserved.

heading.hover: ONLY on interactive headings — Exat design-space names morph specimen weight/width live; Warhol Elvis maps cursor-x to font-size (1.375->2.875em, power3.out 0.3s, return 0.4s). NEVER on prose, body copy, or numbers.
heading.tap: No hover analogue on touch — heading rests at its composed static frame.
heading.focus: Entrance is the state that matters: characterful SplitText (color-cycle back.out / random-skew elastic.out(0.7,0.7)), fired once on enter, reversible on scroll-back in the specimen register.

nav.hover: Per-char rollover (split-rollover, staggered) or scramble-decode on section-nav links (DICH); the bar itself is position:fixed and transparent through scroll — background rgba(0,0,0,0), backdrop-filter:none, no border — at the top AND after scrolling, so the maximal canvas reads through.
nav.tap: Menu toggle drops a full-viewport curtain; links answer with an instant color swap; the bar never solidifies to an opaque brand-border bar.
nav.focus: Links keep a clean accessible name (aria-label) under the per-char split; focus-visible shows the accent state; menu is focus-trapped while open.

cursor.hover: Custom pointer chrome (pointer:fine ONLY) — a lerped/lagging dot or ring (lerp ~0.1-0.2 toward the real pointer position) that morphs by CONTEXT: it grows and surfaces a label ('VIEW' / 'DRAG' / 'OPEN') over media and drag zones, shrinks to a dot over text, and can swap shape/color per section (DICH runs three variants: landing minimal-hypnotic, case denser-electric, transitions barely-there glimmer). Cuberto morphs to a labelled contextual state over media; Warhol/Exat drive type from the same pointer position. This is the archetype's defining hover affordance — the pointer chrome is a first-class element, not only a trail/field channel.
cursor.tap: No custom cursor on touch (pointer:coarse) — the chrome is hidden entirely; the affordance it signalled degrades to the tap/press answer of the underlying element.
cursor.focus: Cursor chrome is decorative and never carries keyboard focus (the element's own focus-visible does). Any label the cursor surfaces on hover must also be reachable without the pointer — no hover-only content trapped behind the cursor state.

mobile_answer: Pointer classes go dormant, press + scroll carry the load. Cursor FIELDS freeze to static composed grids (Exat 'touch devices receive static grid versions'); cursor TRAILS, pointer-parallax, and the custom cursor chrome go dormant/hidden; the coordinate HUD hides <768px (DICH). Press-class elements answer the tap with a flash/press floor 90-160ms; the CTA fill or hard-press offset-shadow IS the tap answer (magnetic pull is a no-op). Depth that came from the pointer now comes from SCROLL — kinetic type keeps its scroll-driven channel so the maximal floor survives. Swap the desktop hold-and-drag/proximity gallery for a native scroll-snap swipe track with tap-to-enlarge (the scored Mobile Excellence line). Any audio stays muted until an explicit gesture and behind a persistent toggle. The single peak degrades to a strong composed static frame, never a sub-30fps render — jurors test on real devices and 'sites that break on iPhone lose immediately'.

gaps.mechanic: A grid of glyphs/words where each unit's variable-font axis + color is driven by Euclidean distance from the cursor to its center. 7 concentric distance rings map to font-weight 200->900 and a hex-lerped color (e.g. #0000cb outer -> #FF0B00 inner); viewport-gated rAF loop (~16ms), promoted layers, no per-frame layout. Touch fallback = static composed grid. This is the archetype's signature mid-page spectacle and powers the currently-MISSING specimen-grid recipe form. No manifest component drives per-unit variable-font axes by pointer distance.

The pointer chrome itself as a first-class element (distinct from the trail/field channels): a lerped/lagging dot or ring (lerp ~0.1-0.2 toward the real pointer) that morphs by context — grows + surfaces a label over media/drag zones, shrinks over text, swaps shape/color per section. pointer:fine only; hidden on touch. The archetype's defining hover affordance had no state row before revision 2 (now added to element_states.cursor); flagged here because no manifest component ships the contextual pointer chrome.

The SATURATED-register per-section color rotation, NOT the archetype's universal color rule — it rests on ONE corpus winner (DICH) plus Figma; the other seven corpus sites are B&W, single-hue, 2-hue, or cream monochrome. The single-accent token contract (--ad-accent) cannot express it: a form/token pattern where each section claims its own accent (and optional ground) from a rotation array, driven by an IntersectionObserver that swaps --ad-accent (and companion CSS vars) as each section enters, so components inherit the section's color world with no per-component change. Optional per-section 'visual temperature' (warm/cool ground). Needed ONLY for the saturated / warm-maximal register — do not apply it to kinetic-register builds.

seen_in: Ponpon Mania (SOTM — per-transition WebGL shader mixes, confirmed this run)
gaps.mechanic: A between-view spectacle channel the scroll-within-page momentum model does not cover: on route/view change, blend the outgoing and incoming scenes through a custom shader mix driven by a GSAP tween (Ponpon renders previous+next WebGL pages and mixes in real time), or a morphing curtain/wipe (21 TSI). For multi-route maximal sites the transition is peak-adjacent — add it as one channel in the momentum floor for multi-view builds. Touch/reduced-motion: degrade to a fast crossfade or instant cut, never a sub-30fps blocking blend. The momentum model was scroll-within-page only; it had no between-view grammar.

A characterful SplitText entrance distinct from the tier's monochrome line/char masks (kinetic-reveal, char-assemble): per-char scale 0->1 with a warm single-hue array (Warhol #FB4E2B ×7 + #FFE5D5, back.out, 0.1s stagger — a single-hue reveal, NOT a multi-hue cycle) OR per-char enter from x:100% with skewX random(-25,25) + rotation 5 + elastic.out(0.7,0.7) + 0.06s stagger (Ponpon), reversible on scroll-back. Keeps an accessible name via aria-label. The archetype's display-type signature; our current SplitText components are monochrome and non-characterful.

A maximalist cursor/idle channel: images or particles spawn at the cursor position as it moves (throttled by travel distance), each spawn tweens scale 0->1 + a filter decay (brightness/contrast 300%->100%) then opacity 1->0 over ~0.4s with a delay; z-index recycling prevents stacking. Eloy's variant is a contact/connect-CTA clone-storm (the 'CLICK TO CONNECT' button spawns 2 clones per 200px of pointer travel, up to 200, mix-blend-mode:difference, staggered enter/exit back.in(1.7)) at the page close — NOT a hero CTA. Fine-pointer only; dormant on touch. Our ambient-idle does not do cursor-spawn trails; this is a footer/idle spectacle channel.

An operable specimen widget: sliders write live CSS custom properties (--ff/--fs/--fw/--lh/--ls) onto a preview block so the visitor drives the type. Already flagged type-tester in recipes.json (specimen-tour-exat) but has no component. The operable-proof beat in the specimen-tour macrostructure; pairs beside cursor-proximity-typefield.

seen_in: Ponpon Mania (SOTM, velocity feedback + shader mixes)
gaps.mechanic: A décor channel driven by scroll VELOCITY (not position). TYPE variant: large numerals/glyphs oscillate in a sine-wave whose amplitude tracks scroll speed (Exat); or a rendered object's position gets a velocity*0.01 feedback nudge (Ponpon). MEDIA variant: the same scroll-velocity signal drives RGB-shift/displacement distortion on imagery/surfaces (21 TSI cursor-distortion + WebGL displacement; Ponpon per-transition shader mixes) — a distinct channel from the position-bound scrubbed reveals, applied to surfaces not just type. Compositor-only, viewport-gated. Our scrubbed channels bind to scroll POSITION; none read velocity.

An opt-in audio channel for sensory-maximal builds: muted by default, a single persistent mute/sound toggle (fixed, always reachable), UI/interaction SFX and/or an ambient bed unlocked on first user gesture (browsers block autoplay). Reduced-motion / data-saver / touch: audio stays off until explicitly enabled; the toggle state persists across the session. A real Awwwards channel for maximal builds, but sourced to a SINGLE boundary corpus member (21 TSI) — thin evidence; ship only when the brief sells sensory maximalism.

unverified: Cuberto is the file's weakest-verified entry: cuberto.com's own Awwwards Site of the Day is real but dates to Jun 22 2018 (7.37 — outside the 2024-2026 window), and the Developer Award is NOT shown on the award page (awwwards.com/sites/cuberto). Multiple other cuberto entries are Nominee/Honorable Mention. Every Cuberto-specific amplitude in element_states.cta (dome-fill timings, expo curve, magnetic pull) and the custom-cursor spec is carried-verified from a prior run's live-CSS read, not re-fetched this run — load-bearing for the CTA + cursor state canon.

Mat Voyce: Awwwards Site of the Day + FWA Site of the Day + Webby honouree + Awwwards Site of the Month nominee (Jan 2025) are confirmed this run. The 'GSAP Site of the Year 2025 nominee' claim appears only in the Uncommon studio writeup and is NOT confirmed at the GSAP award body — treat as studio-claimed, not award-verified. F37 Judge / cream #FFFEF8 are design micro-details, not independently confirmed.

The Bold-Maximal Spectacle-Momentum Law is a synthesized design heuristic, not an award-body measurement. The peak-count-of-one cap IS a corpus observation (no verified winner stacks a second spectacle equal to its signature moment). But the specific '4-5 continuous channels' count and the 'among the highest continuation floor of any archetype' ranking are extrapolations across the corpus, not measured against a scored juror rubric. Defensible as design theory; do not present with the certainty of award-body fact.

The '4-6 colors per section' / per-section color rotation is NOT the archetype's universal color rule — it rests on a SINGLE corpus winner (DICH) plus a hand-wave to Figma. The other seven corpus sites are B&W (Ponpon mostly monochrome, 21 TSI strictly monochromatic), single-hue warm (Warhol #FB4E2B), 2-hue (Exat blue->red), cream monochrome (Mat Voyce), or glitch/brutalist (Eloy). Filed as a saturated-register expression (see the section-accent-rotation gap, downgraded to priority 2), not archetype canon.

21 TSI is a BOUNDARY member: strictly monochromatic (Codrops), kinetic-maximal on the motion axis, not the saturated-color register. Included only as a witness that the constant-motion floor holds outside saturated color; a purist reading files it under kinetic/brutalist. Not saturated-color canon.

Exat's exact Awwwards SOTD month is not pinned this run, but all three awards are confirmed (Awwwards SOTD page live, FWA case at thefwa.com/cases/exat-typeface-p2, CSSDA Website of the Month at cssdesignawards.com/wotm/exat-typeface/47246, scored 8.83); the earlier over-hedge on Exat's awards is resolved.

Nite Riot (BL/S®, Awwwards SOTD 7.64, 'minimalism gets a wild side', Difference blend mode, B&W) was evaluated and EXCLUDED from the core corpus — its restrained B&W palette makes it a weak bold-maximal fit (closer to brutalist-kinetic); noted here as an adjacent case, not evidence.

Jam the Chaos (Elvis Mao, SITCON 2026, Three.js/GSAP/Astro, 'rhythm in chaos', vote 9.1) is an Awwwards NOMINEE (2026-06-27), not yet a SOTD/SOTM/HM winner at time of research — excluded from the corpus per the award-verification bar; a strong future candidate if it wins.

DICH/Warhol per-button CTA hover states were not documented in their Codrops case studies (which focused on cursor/scroll/loader mechanics); the CTA element_states are grounded in Cuberto's carried-verified live-CSS canon + the fill-invert-cta manifest canon, not in DICH/Warhol button teardowns. Magnetic-CTA-hover is likewise Cuberto-sourced and inherits that carried-verified status.
variation: This section_playbook is one legal costume of the archetype, never THE skeleton. Structure is story-native (SKILL.md Phase 1): the body's sections derive from the universe's spine, then check against these roles for coverage — never the reverse. The axes serial winners measurably rotate between builds (21-artifact corpus, 5 studios): body content archetype + item counts, the ONE signature device (never reused across builds), the close mechanism, the hero medium, the index/HUD costume. What persists as DNA: type grammar, motion register + interaction vocabulary, annotation grammar as a form, engineering architecture. The same content archetype + item count + close mechanism recurring across two different-brand builds has zero winner precedent.
